findings.description: When ANSI is stripped, the code calls `.strip()` on the whole prompt text, which also removes legitimate leading/trailing whitespace. The prompt text normally ends with a separator such as a trailing space (e.g. "Name: ").
findings.rationale: Trigger: any prompt on a non-tty or non-color stream (piped output, CliRunner, redirected stdout). The prompt is built with a trailing space suffix. After `.strip()`, `input("Name:")` shows "Name:" with no space, so the user's typed text runs against the prompt. This differs from the colored path and from echo behavior, which preserves the whitespace.
